focus: Default-on integration needs, cost and risk
noveltyJustification: Tied the measured column's validity window to the exact artifacts it is bound to (model tuple, option-set hash, unpinned rows) and reframed integration cost as a critical-path latency multiplier rather than a token problem.
keyQuestions: Q5: What would a default-on integration need, cost and risk?
answeredQuestions: Q5: What would a default-on integration need, cost and risk?

summary: Serving is operator-gated and out of scope for this phase; the deliverable is a ranked brief for a later build phase.
Fleet policy already exists (D1: Jev only, dormant unless auth passes, no secret) and the scorer gate mirrors it; serving substrate exists (cli-jev transport, JEV_TRANSPORT measured adopt).
A call at p50 330 ms roughly doubles the entire 200 ms cold-lookup Gate 1 budget, making latency the headline integration cost; no-hit-only or advisory triggers are the mitigations.
The verdict is bound to jev 0.6.2/official/jev-1.13.0 and the optionSetSha256 of track descriptions; requalification is print-only, so rollout needs an explicit requalification trigger.
Default-on converts Gate 1's fail-open no-hit into a wrong-answer mode while row accuracy is 37.9 percent (48.7 percent on decided rows); a confidence/no-hit gate is required.
